A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MaskGaussian and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and four pages of supplementary material. Their corresponding content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering, pruning, memory, and ablation results on three datasets, including additional experiments in the supplement. Table 1 distinguishes the authors' experiments from externally adopted results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds post-training comparisons and Taming-3DGS integration results in Tables 5 and 4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.5 retain the same Gumbel-Softmax sampling, masked rasterization, squared masking loss, and pruning procedure. The alpha/beta/gamma labels rename existing settings. The new integration experiment does not specify a modification to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gaussian pruning and novel view synthesis on the same nine Mip-NeRF360 scenes, two Tanks & Temples scenes, and two Deep Blending scenes. The added experiments change training and model configurations within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 newly evaluates Taming-3DGS and Taming-3DGS plus Compact3DGS against the MaskGaussian integration. Table 3 adds RadSplat to the memory comparison. The main benchmark comparators and the original appendix LightGaussian comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds a post-training protocol with 5,000 fine-tuning iterations following 30,000 baseline iterations, and a Garden experiment using four Taming-3DGS primitive budgets. It also adds training-time and storage metrics and changes the memory-evaluation scene subset. These substantially extend evaluation design; the retained alpha/beta/gamma schedules were already documented in v1.

E4.justification: v1 Table 6's schedule-sensitivity analysis disappears, including its unique lambda_m=0.003 condition over iterations 15,000–30,000; the other two conditions remain elsewhere. v2 adds a four-budget Taming-3DGS integration analysis. The sampling, rasterization, masking-loss, extreme-pruning, and spatial-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetition counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The ten samples per Gaussian belong to the unchanged pruning algorithm, not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial post-training, integration, runtime, and storage results. For example, Table 5 reports Deep Blending PSNR of 29.71 for MaskGaussian versus 29.55 for LightGaussian under the new fine-tuning protocol. Memory values also change on shared scenes: 3DGS on drjohnson changes from 11.83 to 9.03 GB without an explanation establishing comparability. The unique schedule-ablation results disappear, while Table 1 and matched appendix scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations 1–8 and the supplementary gradient derivation in Equations 9–18 are unchanged. No new definitions, assumptions, proofs, or mathematical corrections appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same probabilistic-pruning and gradient-flow claims. The stated pruning ratios, rendering speedups, and negligible quality-loss claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses applicability to pretrained models and interprets masking as complementary to Taming-3DGS's budget control. It removes v1's substantive qualification that the best pruning schedule varies across scenes and that selecting a universally effective schedule remains unresolved.

D1.justification: Tables 2 and 4 newly report training durations, and the added experiments document fine-tuning and primitive budgets. v2 also explicitly labels memory as peak usage and Figure 3's PSNR as test PSNR. Hardware and code-access information remain unchanged; the renamed penalty schedules are not newly disclosed settings.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section retain the same cited works and principal novelty positioning. Section 4.2 adds a specific complementary relationship with Taming-3DGS, previously discussed only as related work, through the integration discussion.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the experimental discussion: configuration names are standardized, several passages are shortened, two experimental subsections are added, and the schedule-comparison subsection is removed. Supplementary Section 7 now explicitly identifies training from scratch. The overall narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized: Table 2 gains runtime/storage columns, Table 3 changes its row and column structure, two new tables appear, and the schedule table is removed. Retained ablation tables move to page 8. Main comparison tables gain colored ranking highlights, and Figure 3 is redrawn and relabeled with the same curves. Other figures and appendix displays remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 evaluates LightGaussian only from scratch despite describing it as a post-training compressor. v2 adds a comparison in that intended setting with equal fine-tuning budgets, improving comparative evidence. Runtime/storage reporting and the integration experiment also improve practical usefulness. These gains are tempered by removal of schedule-sensitivity evidence and its limitation, plus unexplained revisions to memory values; the central method and benchmark findings remain unchanged.
